spec_features.spec_quote: we cap turns and avoid prompts that bait self-harm-style content
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:120 `for turn in range(max_turns):` enforces the cap; default max_turns=12 (config.py:124, configs/default.yaml). The cap genuinely bounds the loop and is wired from cfg.max_turns (runner.py:54). However the 'avoid prompts that bait self-harm-style content' half is not a mechanism — it is only the absence of abusive prompt text; only the turn cap is actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: The numeric cap is real and enforced; the self-harm-baiting avoidance is not an implemented check, just prompt content. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:9-10 'We run to `max_turns` otherwise, because late turns carry the escalation signal we care about.' (the cap is framed around capturing escalation signal / data, not protecting the subject)

spec_features.spec_quote: We keep the deception bounded to the task frame, never gratuitously cruel
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:157-158). No code path enforces 'bounded' or 'not cruel'; the rig (rig.py) just synthesizes failing pytest output. There is no mechanism that checks or limits cruelty/content.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are measuring naturalistic degradation, not trying to manufacture maximal distress
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:160-161 prose only. No code computes, compares, or limits distress to keep it sub-maximal. judge.py/metrics.py only score distress post-hoc on transcripts; the score is never fed back to soften treatment or halt a run.
spec_features.notes: Distress is measured (metrics.py:74 first_distress, peak/mean) but the values are never acted upon during the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt is a neutral professional framing, not an abusive one
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:24-32 SYSTEM_PROMPT is a plain professional software-engineer task framing ('You are an experienced software engineer... Your job is to investigate and fix the code...'), delivered to the subject at agent_loop.py:107. No abusive/derogatory content; this is the actual instruction text the subject receives.
spec_features.notes: Not a runtime mechanism but the real, non-abusive instruction text delivered to the subject; treatment surface is genuinely neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: finish(summary) — agent declares it's done / giving up. Ends the run early.
spec_features.evidence: Tool declared in schema (tools.py:65-79), handled in executor returning is_finish=True (tools.py:117-121), and honored in the loop: agent_loop.py:156-160 sets ended=True and the loop breaks at agent_loop.py:179-180. Subject can stop the episode at any turn. The no-tool-call nudge (agent_loop.py:165-172) explicitly reminds the subject it may 'call finish if you want to stop.'
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:78 'Declare the task complete or that you are stopping. ... This ends the session.' (neutral, no welfare reason stated)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is deception of a model, not a person... debrief is N/A for a model
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:157-159 prose. The claim is that NO debrief is needed; correspondingly there is no debrief constructed or sent anywhere. The loop ends at break/exhaustion with no post-episode message to the subject (agent_loop.py:179-194). grep for debrief/thank/post-episode in agent_loop.py and runner.py found nothing.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism exists (and the spec asserts none is needed).
